notes: Variance-correction constant a = 0.75 (lognormal), 1 otherwise (manual §30.5.2).

[completeness review 2026-10-03] Manual §30.5.2 internal inconsistencies: (1) binomial X prints v0·exp(β0) = π/(1-π), but the stated limit v0 = lim_{β1→0} v1 of its own v1 formula gives 1/(π(1-π)); a scratch check (not reference evidence) of the Signorini column of Table 2 for Bin(0.2) reproduces 0.321 and 0.788 only with 1/(π(1-π)). (2) normal X prints v1·exp(β0) = exp(-[β1µ + (β1σ)²/2]) while v0·exp(β0) = 1/σ²; the limit requires a factor 1/σ² (no effect for σ = 1). (3) The exponential density in §30.1 is garbled ('(1/λ)e^(-1/λ)'); the MGF (1 - x/λ)^-1 in §30.5.2 implies a rate parameter λ (mean 1/λ) - verify the X parm λ meaning by capture before using the Exp(3) rows of Table 2.

[second review pass 2026-10-03] With the §30.5.2 exponential formulas (v0·exp(β0) = λ², v1·exp(β0) = (λ − β1)³/λ) and the Signorini equations (16)-(17), reading 'Exp(3)' as rate λ = 3 reproduces the Table 2 Signorini column (0.649 and 0.952 for β1 = −0.4 and −0.7); reading 3 as the mean (rate 1/3) gives 1.000 (scratch arithmetic in R 4.6.1, not reference evidence). This supports the rate reading of the manual's formulas; the meaning of the UI field 'X parm λ' still has to be captured. The previous review's Bin(0.2) finding (only v0·exp(β0) = 1/(π(1 − π)) reproduces 0.321 and 0.788) was re-checked and holds; N(0,1), β1 = −0.1 also reproduces 0.443.

notes: 'Exact' mode uses the model-based asymptotic standard error, not an exact finite-sample standard error (manual §31.5.1).
Output also usable to perform the observed test (manual §31.3) - an observed-analysis use, separate from planning.

[completeness review 2026-10-03] Manual uses two different cell-probability estimators: §31.1 (drawer, C.I. from frequencies) p_ij = (f_ij + 0.5)/(N + 2), §31.5.2 (approximation mode) p̂_ij = (f_ij + 0.5)/N. The Fig. 37 drawer values (Est. marginal prob x = 0.6122449 = 60/98 for N = 96) are consistent with (N + 2) in exact mode; the frequency-drawer estimator remains a separate scope from the independently checked forward-power approximation. §31.3 says the C.I. border is used 'as ... ρ under H0' where H1 is meant.

[second review pass 2026-10-03] Manual §31.5.1 prints the first term of the Pearson standard error as (a + d)(b + d)/4 (frequency form) and (p11 + p22)(p12 + p22)/4 (probability form); the Brown and Benedetti form (a + d)(b + c)/4 reproduces DOC-229 'Std err r' = 0.074465 exactly at ρ = 0, N = 463 and the printed marginals, whereas the printed term gives 0.083673 (scratch arithmetic in R 4.6.1, not reference evidence). The same lines write Φ1, Φ2 with the density symbol ϕ although the normal CDF is required (the reproduction used the CDF). Confirmed on the rendered page 83.
[live capture 2026-10-05] Inventory certified against the running G*Power 3.1.9.7 (Wine emulator_capture); differences from the provisional entry are listed in live_capture.differences.

2026-10-07 clarification: manual rows Y/columns X require the first-term correction (a+d)(b+c)/4 and normal CDFs; the earlier Phi swap reflects transposed orientation. Exact and Bonett-Price modes have independent and captured comparisons (validation/independent/g7 and validation/compare/z_tetrachoric_correlation). Extreme margins, frequency-estimator ambiguity and uncompleted native/reference branches remain separately documented.
